name: pypilot-vscode
description: Sets up Python environments, resolves version and hardware compatibility without external AI or API keys.

commands.title: PyPilot: Migrate Conda environment.yml to pyproject.toml

pypilot.helperPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a `pypilot` executable to use instead of the downloaded engine, for example a local build (`target/release/pypilot`). When set, PyPilot runs exactly this binary (it must answer `--version`), never downloads the engine and does not offer engine updates. Leave empty to use the engine pinned by this extension.

enumDescriptions: Offer only the engine version this extension release was tested with (its pin). Updating the extension brings newer engines.
Also offer newer engine releases from GitHub as soon as they are published. Each download is verified against the release's SHA256SUMS file; releases without one are not installed.
pypilot.engineUpdates.markdownDescription: Which PyPilot engine updates to offer. Downloads are always checked against a SHA-256 before anything is extracted.

enumDescriptions: Auto (default): Uses uv if installed on system PATH, prompts to install if missing, or falls back to pip. pixi projects (pixi.toml, or [tool.pixi.workspace] in pyproject.toml) always use pixi.
Use uv-accelerated pip-compatible mode (requirements.txt only via uv venv and uv pip).
Use standard pip + python -m venv. Never touches uv.
Use pixi: the environment lives in .pixi/envs/<name> (see pypilot.pixiEnvironment), installs go through `pixi add --pypi`, and PyPilot never creates a .venv or edits pixi.lock.
pypilot.packageManager.description: Package manager for environment creation and installs.

enumDescriptions: Toast for every finding, including informational notes.
Only toast for warnings and errors.
pypilot.notifications.description: Controls when PyPilot shows automatic notifications on workspace open.

pypilot.autoCheckOnOpen.description: Automatically scan the workspace when it is first opened.

pypilot.autoSelectVenv.description: Make the workspace's .venv (in pixi projects: the pixi environment named by pypilot.pixiEnvironment, .pixi/envs/<name>) the active Python interpreter (and so the recommended notebook kernel) when it is created or changed, and on startup when no interpreter inside the workspace is selected. Requires the Python extension. The "PyPilot: Use Project Environment" command works regardless of this setting.

pypilot.pixiEnvironment.patternErrorMessage: pixi environment names use lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
pypilot.pixiEnvironment.markdownDescription: Which pixi environment PyPilot and the interpreter selection use in multi-environment pixi projects (the `[environments]` table of `pixi.toml`). The interpreter is `.pixi/envs/<name>`; install it with `pixi install -e <name>`. Ignored outside pixi projects.

pypilot.dataRefreshDays.description: How often (in days) to refresh bundled tables. 0 means fully offline.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with PyPilot
walkthroughs.description: From an open folder to a working Python environment, including pixi projects.

steps.title: Open a Python project
steps.description:
PyPilot starts on its own in any folder with Python files or a Python manifest.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

steps.title: PyPilot checks it
steps.description:
Python versions, wheels, CUDA builds and imports are checked when the folder opens. See everything it found in the report.
[Show Environment Report](command:pypilot.doctor)

steps.title: Fix the environment
steps.description:
One command creates or repairs the environment on a supported Python and selects it as the interpreter.
[Set Up Environment](command:pypilot.setup)

steps.title: Using pixi? What's different
steps.description:
In pixi projects the environment is .pixi/envs/<name>, PyPilot never creates a .venv or touches pixi.lock, and installs go through pixi add --pypi.
[Choose pixi Environment](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22pypilot.pixiEnvironment%22%5D)
